![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14243229/assets/b8131b2ca68e378ef96c1b57e655db0a89d6e5207f0ac842612c64b30a963912.png)

The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-2,5].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $1,$ $2$ and $5,$ respectively (from left to right). Find the maximum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-2,5]$ given that $f(1)=-12.$
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the maximum value of $f(x)$ on $[-2,5]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-2,5),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=\pm 1.$ Therefore, the candidates are  $x=-2,-1,1,5.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =-12 \\ f(-1) & =f(1)+{\int }_{1}^{-1}{f}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =f(1)-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{f}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-12-(-2) \\  & =-12+2 \\  & =-10 \\ f(-2) & =f(1)+{\int }_{1}^{-2}{f}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =f(1)-{\int }_{-2}^{1}{f}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-12-(-2+1) \\  & =-12+1 \\  & =-11 \\ f(5) & =f(1)+{\int }_{1}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-12-5 \\  & =-17\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the largest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{max}}=max\{-12,-10,-11,-17\}=-10.
$$

Therefore, the maximum value of $f$ is  ${f}_{\text{max}}=-10,$ and the value of $x$ that maximizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{max}}=-1.$
